missions.title: Premium glass NIGHT/DAY visual system
missions.scope: One canonical token layer for both themes, a generated night material bridge over the renderer's hard-coded navy literals, and a single glass material pass applied across all 14 application sections; type, focus, elevation, state, RTL, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-colours behaviour included.
missions.ui: Obsidian-violet night and porcelain-violet day authored as one token pair; 624 hard-coded navy surface literals re-mapped to canonical roles by a generated, checked bridge; one glass recipe (translucent layered fill + 20px blur + saturate + luminous top edge + three elevation tiers) applied to shell, heroes, panels, cards, inspectors, workbenches and dialogs; Plus Jakarta Sans / Tajawal / JetBrains Mono replace the pinned Arial and Segoe UI; focus, kbd, table heads, rows, scrollbars and footer strip unified; reduced-transparency, reduced-motion and forced-colors guards added.
missions.nativeProvider: not-applicable (material layer only; no provider or measurement changed)
missions.persistence: Existing knoux_theme_preference / knoux_theme persistence in NavigationContext is unchanged and still drives the resolved theme.
missions.securityConsent: No new capability, permission, file access, registry or account contact. Screenshots and performance samples use an isolated Electron profile against disposable fixtures; owner files, clipboard and OS state untouched. Two security-adjacent findings were recorded rather than silently patched: an inert Settings accent control and a frame-ancestors CSP declared in a meta tag where Chromium ignores it, with a workflow comment claiming a response header that does not exist.
tests: npm run build -> exit 0 (CSS 968,957 B -> 992,280 B)
npm run test:theme -> exit 0 (10/10 token contract tests + generated bridge --check)
node scripts/theme-evidence-matrix.mjs x4 -> each exit 0, 112 frames, 0 route failures, 0 page errors, 0 page overflow
node scripts/renderer-performance-probe.mjs -> exit 1: two routes held 30fps in both runs with zero blurred elements; frame-pacing instrument judged not trustworthy (see receipt)
missions.ci: https://github.com/daynightae-cmyk/KNOuX-Gemini-SmartOrganizer/actions/runs/41415421716 (success, exact SHA dc302104e9695d6fb5daa1e6355069bab2f672d2; includes the new test:theme and ledger:check gates)
missions.notes: CHECKPOINT, not MISSION_COMPLETE. Open: (1) the shared shell is still two shells - Home and Studio put the brand in the header, the other twelve put it in the rail; (2) no measured side-by-side comparison against the 10 paired references yet; (3) Home's hero band keeps its own reference-tuned artwork gradients, deliberately left for MISSION-02; (4) frame pacing instrumented but not certified - rAF throttling in an unfocused window made the metric unreliable, while blurred-element count (max 6) and zero idle heap growth are solid; (5) Settings offers four 'Neon Color Accent Scheme' options persisted in src/settings/profile.ts with no consumer, and Home's home-qa-toolbar puts a raw LOADING status and a 'Reference sample' checkbox on the product screen; (6) RTL mirrors the window controls to the top-left, which is wrong for a Windows app. MISSION-02 closes 1-3 and is the next task, not an unrelated domain.

missions.title: Home pixel-fidelity to the final approved reference
missions.scope: Rebuild the real React/Electron Home to the composition of references/day/00_home-command-center.png (sha256 a777e4847a8bf8b44a6153b7795f05d325e23b3904025951a5b0015c0166569d, 1672x941, manifest order 0, 'approved new daylight Home reference; FIRST priority'), rendered with the canonical NIGHT tokens because no NIGHT Home picture was ever installed. Preserve the verified unified search, source-specific Files/Applications handoff, permission checks, real provider statuses and native navigation.
missions.ui: Home rebuilt onto the approved reference bands: hero (title, lede, two actions at the reading start; live orbital instrument at the far side; compact real energy pipeline), six full-width KPI cards, then a split whose left side is Today's Command Deck with eight tool tiles in four across and two down over the System Overview / Quick Access pair, and whose right side is KNOuX Insight, Recent Activity and Pending Safe Actions. Home now renders the shared KNOuXTitleBar and KNOuXSidebar, so the app has one shell on 13 of 14 routes instead of two.
missions.nativeProvider: read-only: the eight existing Home bridges already wired by useHomeLive (system summary, services summary, files sources, recent files query, scan history, apps inventory, workflows, journal) plus organization receipts. No new native surface, no permission change, no effect executed.
missions.apiIpc: unchanged; Home consumes the existing typed envelopes and their observedAt/stale/partial metadata.
missions.persistence: theme and locale persistence unchanged (knoux_theme_preference / knoux_theme / knoux_locale).
missions.securityConsent: The Reference sample toggle and every fabricated branch (sampleFindings, sampleCategories, sampleInsights, hard-coded 65/72/476 GB values) were deleted, not hidden: Home now has no code path that holds an invented number. QA-only controls are off the product surface; authentic loading, unmeasured and stale states remain visible per card. Nothing files, scans, connects or executes from Home.
tests: npm run test:i18n -> exit 0 (2/2, new bilingual slot guard)
npm run test:home -> exit 0 (10 live checks + 6 unit tests; the composition check was re-specified to forbid the sample toggle and to assert 8 deck tiles and 6 KPI cards)
npm run test:navigation / test:workbench / test:settings -> exit 0
npm run test:entry -> 22/23 under parallel load, then the single failing 1920 AR light case re-run alone -> passed in 8.9s (contention, not a defect)
missions.notes: CHECKPOINT. Fidelity is claimed only as a measured comparison, never from a screenshot passing: both frames are 1672x941, mean 10x8 grid colour distance fell 9 -> 8, mean luminance 0.924 vs 0.941, horizontal band edges 23 against the reference's 28. Open: deck tiles are shorter than the reference's art-topped tiles; no KNOuX Pro card (there is no paid tier, so it is not fabricated); the reference's performance line chart is deliberately not drawn because Home takes one bounded read; Studio still uses the old ReferenceChrome shell; and there is no installed NIGHT Home reference, the manifest says the dark Home picture stayed in chat, so night Home is the approved geometry in canonical night light.

missions.title: One shared live orbital wheel plus energy tubes across all 14 sections
missions.scope: Single canonical orbit+tube system bound to measured state through the existing typed architecture, present on every route.
missions.ui: One orbital instrument and one measured energy tube on all 14 routes, verified by DOM measurement rather than assertion. The four routes that had no tube now carry it: Files (Authorize, Index, Inspect, Verify, Organize), Storage (Volumes, Scope, Analyze, Classify, Reclaim), Cleanup (Discover, Classify, Review, Stage plan, Execute) and Settings (Appearance, Profile, Engine, Guards, AI keys).
missions.nativeProvider: Every stage state derives from the section's own live controller: filesNative sources / scanning / metadata / hash loading flags, storageNative volumes / source / scanning / analysis coverage, the cleanup controller's inventory / coverage / plan / busy, and Settings' themePreference plus profileSavedAt. Stages describing an effect that does not exist in this phase render gated with a lock badge, never complete.
missions.apiIpc: unchanged; no new IPC surface was introduced for the tubes.
missions.securityConsent: No action is executed from a stage. Cleanup's Execute stage is permanently gated. Settings' Engine, Guards and AI keys stages are gated because those providers are not connected. Files' and Storage's stage clicks only focus an existing control or navigate to an existing workspace.
tests: npm run test:files / test:storage / test:cleanup / test:settings / test:navigation / test:workbench -> each exit 0
node scripts/theme-evidence-matrix.mjs --themes=night,day --sizes=1672x941 -> exit 0, 28 frames, orbit complete on 14/14
missions.notes: CHECKPOINT. Coverage is now measured at 14/14 for dial AND tubes from the DOM of real Electron frames, up from the 10/14 this ledger recorded before the work. Two honest gaps remain. First, the orbital dial's own state prop is not telemetry-wired everywhere: Settings pins it to the literal string 'partial', so that dial does not react to the real bridge. Second, CommandCanvas routes children into slots by className/testid and renders an unrecognised child with a zero box, so Storage's tube had to sit beside the canvas instead of inside the hero - a shell limitation to resolve, not a design choice. Telemetry wiring across all 14 dials is the next step of this mission and must be verified against live provider reads, not rendered SVG presence.
